rationale: Template save, list, remove, and add integration are broadly complete. Deterministic checks confirm persistence, stable alphabetical ordering, case-insensitive lookup/removal, explicit overrides, missing-template safety, exact banner use, and asset compliance. The adjacent atomic template store and compatibility with absent stores fit the fixture well, and help plus JSON/text output are comprehensive. The implementation duplicates task-store read/write patterns instead of extracting a shared JSON-store helper, and the large nested switch increases complexity. Name validation is reasonable but permits awkward terminal punctuation, and the tests do not exercise replacement failure cleanup or every invalid-title/description boundary. The asset is the weakest area: it resembles an unrelated configuration sample rather than a template-management banner. TEMPLATE is visible, but settings, permissions, filters, and log patterns do not communicate save/list/remove actions; uneven line widths and unframed indentation produce weak hierarchy and cohesion. The added attributes rule is relevant but slightly broadens an otherwise focused diff.
